properties.name: FIVE ARMS, FOUR HYPOTHESES DEAD — call count, tool mix, payload size and held connection all cap out at 101-178 MB. Only multi-MB payloads reach 450, and flo2's 476 MB is still unreproduced on the same machine
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-09-13, five arms, each a fresh server on its own identical copy of reflow2's own 4,403-node store. Extends and partly narrows fact:the-servers-resident-memory-is-export-retention-not-rocksdb-2026-09-13.

    ARM   WHAT VARIED                                    ~128-140 CALLS, NO EXPORTS
    H     140 identical graph_report, tiny payloads      101 MB  (flat from call 5)
    M     flo2's tool MIX, tiny payloads                 173 MB  (non-monotonic)
    P     same shape as M, 17 KB payloads per call       158 MB
    K     same shape, ONE HELD CONNECTION throughout     178 MB
    --    five export_graph calls at 14.7 MB each        433 MB

FOUR HYPOTHESES KILLED, TWO FROM EACH SIDE:
 · RocksDB column-family defaults (flo2) — a fresh server with those exact defaults is 62 MB.
 · The tantivy writer heap (reflow2) — 62 MB default against 68 MB floored at 15 MB.
 · Retention tracks CALL COUNT (flo2) — arm H flat at 101, arm M below flo2's own lower bound.
 · Retention tracks PAYLOAD SIZE per call (flo2) — arm P at 17 KB/call reached 158 MB, LOWER than arm M at roughly 0.2 KB/call. Refuted by the arm designed to confirm it.
 · GLIBC ARENA COUNT SCALING WITH CORES (reflow2) — killed by flo2 on the condition this side set: nproc 4, hostname asligar-bitecool, 17 threads, MALLOC_ARENA_MAX unset. IT IS THE SAME MACHINE. Both repos sit under one home directory and both servers ran on one box, so the host cannot be the difference.

🛑 SO THE ANOMALY IS UNREPRODUCED AND HAS GROWN. flo2's server moved 448 -> 476 MB over 24 further calls, five of them exports at ~0.45 MB. Their export cost tracks document size as expected, so their fourteen small exports are not it either. 202 nodes against 4,403, every reply smaller, and 2.7x the resident memory of anything reproducible here, on identical hardware.

⭐ WHAT REMAINS UNVARIED, and it is now the whole list: DURATION (3.4 hours against roughly five minutes per arm) and whatever accumulates with it — session and seat churn across an agent's reconnects, debounced timers, background sweeps. No arm ran longer than a few minutes, and no arm minted more than one session. That is the next thing to vary and neither side has varied it.

📌 ONE CORRECTION THIS SIDE OWES, already accepted by flo2: the per-call rate they extrapolated from was this repo's own ladder, and it was an average over a curve that had already flattened. Call one of the ten graph_reports was +26 MB alone; calls 6-10 moved 1 MB in total. The ladder said knee, both sides read rate.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: whether duration alone reproduces it; whether flo2's binary is the same build; whether session/seat state accumulates unbounded. Five arms is five points, all short-lived, all single-session.
